article.title: Using XPath
article.p: This section describes how to use SaxonC as a library for XPath processing from C/C++, Python and PHP, without making any use of XSLT stylesheets. It includes information on the XPath API, and the API for the SaxonC implementation of the XPath object model. On other pages you will find the APIs for XSLT transformation, the APIs for running XQuery, and the APIs for schema validation.
For information about the different ways of loading source documents, see Handling XML documents.

div.p: SaxonC supports APIs for XPath processing on C/C++, Python and PHP.
For a general overview on using XPath see details in the main Saxon documentation. A good starting place is the section Representation of XDM values.

section.title: From a C application
section.p: In this section we give a tutorial of how to setup a C API application. In SaxonCProcessor.h we have several functions to execute XPath expressions. Please note the compile phase happens within the same execute function call. There are functions to output the results to an XDM type given as the struct sxn_value. The XML document sources and execution file are supplied as arguments to the function, but users may find it useful to supply parameters and properties using the structs sxnc_parameter and sxnc_property, respectively.
The first step is the memory allocation of the processor and variables required by SaxonC. To simplify the process we have the utility function initSaxonc() to alloc the following variables:

ul.li: environ - SaxonC environment given as the struct sxnc_environment
processor - The SaxonC Processor data structure given as the struct sxnc_processor which is used as a reference to the Java Saxon Processor object in Java

parameters - The sxnc_parameter struct as an array is used to represent the the parameters required by the XSLT processors. For example stylesheet parameters can be supplied here. See further details here.
properties - The sxnc_property struct as an array is used to represent the properties required by the XSLT processors. See full list of properties here.

section.title: From a C++ application
section.p: The SaxonC C++ interface is custom-designed API for XPath processing, allowing integrated access to all Saxon's XML processing capabilities in a uniform way. The C++ also provides the internal API on which we build the Python and PHP APIs.
You can evaluate an XPath expression using the C++ interface in a number of ways, for instance as follows:

li.p: Create a SaxonProcessor and set any global configuration options on the SaxonProcessor.

Build the source document by calling newDocumentBuilder() to create a document builder, setting appropriate options, and then calling either the parseXmlFromString() and parseXmlFromFile() method. This returns an XdmNode which can be supplied as the context item to the XPath expression. The SaxonProcessor also has one-shot parse methods which can be used for simple cases where no options are required.
Call newXPathProcessor() to create an XPathProcessor, and set any options that are local to a specific compilation (notably declaring namespace prefixes that are used in the XPath expression).
Set any options required for the specific XPath execution on the XPathProcessor (for example, the initial context node, the values of any variables referenced in the expression).

To compile and evaluate the expression, call one of the methods evaluate(), evaluateSingle() or effectiveBooleanValue to execute the XPath expression. These are compile-and-go methods to execute an expression directly without going through an explicit compilation process provides a simpler approach if the expression is only evaluated once.

The result of an XPath expression is in general an XdmValue, representing a value as defined in the XDM data model (that is, a sequence of nodes and/or atomic values). Subclasses of XdmValue include XdmItem, XdmNode, and XdmAtomicValue, and these relate directly to the corresponding concepts in XDM. Various methods are available to translate between this model and native C++ data types.

section.p: Examples of the use of the C++ API to evaluate XPath expressions are included in the SaxonC download file in the directory samples/cppTests, see file testXPath.cpp.

section.title: From a Python application
section.p: The SaxonC Python interface is custom-designed API for XPath processing, allowing integrated access to all Saxon's XML processing capabilities in a uniform way. The Python API is directly built upon the C++ API for XPath.
You can evaluate an XPath expression using the Python interface in a number of ways, for instance as follows:

li.p: Create a PySaxonProcessor and set any global configuration options on the PySaxonProcessor.

Build the source document by calling new_document_builder() to create a document builder, setting appropriate options, and then calling either the parse_xml_from_string() and parse_xml_from_file() method. This returns an PyXdmNode which can be supplied as the context item to the XPath expression. The PySaxonProcessor also has one-shot parse methods which can be used for simple cases where no options are required.
Call new_xpath_processor() to create an PyXPathProcessor, and set any options that are local to a specific compilation (notably declaring namespace prefixes that are used in the XPath expression).
Set any options required for the specific XPath execution on the PyXPathProcessor (for example, the initial context node, the values of any variables referenced in the expression).

To compile and evaluate the expression, call one of the methods evaluate(), evaluate_single() or effective_boolean_value to execute the XPath expression. These are compile-and-go methods to execute an expression directly without going through an explicit compilation process provides a simpler approach if the expression is only evaluated once.

The result of an XPath expression is in general an PyXdmValue, representing a value as defined in the XDM data model (that is, a sequence of nodes and/or atomic values). Subclasses of XdmValue include PyXdmItem, PyXdmNode, and PyXdmAtomicValue, and these relate directly to the corresponding concepts in XDM. Various methods are available to translate between this model and native Python data types.

section.p: Examples of the use of the Python API to evaluate XPath expressions are included in the SaxonC download file in the directory pypi, see files test_saxonc.py and also the test driver in testsuite_driver/xslt30_test_suite_driver.py.

section.title: From a PHP application
section.p: The SaxonC PHP interface is custom-designed API for XPath processing, allowing integrated access to all Saxon's XML processing capabilities in a uniform way. The PHP API is directly built upon the PHP API for XPath.
You can evaluate an XPath expression using the PHP interface in a number of ways, for instance as follows:

li.p: Create a Saxon\SaxonProcessor which lives in the Saxon namespace and set any global configuration options on the SaxonProcessor.

Build the source document by calling newDocumentBuilder() to create a document builder, setting appropriate options, and then calling either the parseXmlFromString() and parseXmlFromFile() method. This returns an Saxon\XdmNode which can be supplied as the context item to the XPath expression. The SaxonProcessor also has one-shot parse methods which can be used for simple cases where no options are required.
Call newXPathProcessor() to create an Saxon\XPathProcessor, and set any options that are local to a specific compilation (notably declaring namespace prefixes that are used in the XPath expression).
Set any options required for the specific XPath execution on the XPathProcessor (for example, the initial context node, the values of any variables referenced in the expression).

To compile and evaluate the expression, call one of the methods evaluate(), evaluateSingle() or effectiveBooleanValue to execute the XPath expression. These are compile-and-go methods to execute an expression directly without going through an explicit compilation process provides a simpler approach if the expression is only evaluated once.

The result of an XPath expression is in general an Saxon\XdmValue, representing a value as defined in the XDM data model (that is, a sequence of nodes and/or atomic values). Subclasses of XdmValue include Saxon\XdmItem, Saxon\XdmNode, and Saxon\XdmAtomicValue, and these relate directly to the corresponding concepts in XDM. Various methods are available to translate between this model and native Python data types.

section.p: Examples of the use of the PHP API to evaluate XPath expressions are included in the SaxonC download file in the directory samples/php, see files xpathExamples.php.

section.title: XdmNode Navigation
section.p: The XdmNode class provides DOM like methods to navigation the nodes in the tree. The options available in C++, Python and PHP APIs are as follows:

li.p: In the C++ and Python APIs we can navigate the tree using the getChildren() method which returns all the child nodes at a given parent node. For PHP the getChildNode() method requires an integer index argument, which we can use with the getChildCount() method to navigate the child nodes. We also have the methods getParent() navigate back up the tree and the method getAttributeNodes() and getAttributeValue(name) to retrieve the attribute nodes.

In SaxonC 12.3, as an alternative to option 1. we have the method axisNodes() which provides a more powerful navigation to traverse the tree according to a tree axis. Axis options are as follows: ANCESTOR, ANCESTOR_OR_SELF, ATTRIBUTE, CHILD, DESCENDANT, DESCENDANT_OR_SELF, FOLLOWING, FOLLOWING_SIBLING, NAMESPACE, PARENT, PRECEDING, PRECEDING_SIBLING and SELF.
